takeaway: Trendelenburg gait means weak hip abductors, the gluteus medius and minimus: the opposite hip dips and the trunk lurches over the weak side.

question.text: A 67-year-old man walks into your orthopaedic clinic after his total hip replacement and you notice he has a Trendelenburg gait. Which muscles are most likely to have been damaged to cause this type of gait?
question.say: A sixty-seven-year-old man walks into your orthopaedic clinic after his total hip replacement and you notice he has a Trendelenburg gait. Which muscles are most likely to have been damaged to cause this type of gait?

lines.text: After his hip replacement, this man walks with a Trendelenburg gait.
This gait comes from weak hip abductors.
And the hip abductors are the gluteus medius and gluteus minimus, here fast asleep.
lines.say: (laugh) And the hip abductors are the gluteus medius and gluteus minimus, here fast asleep.

lines.text: If the right abductors are weak, lifting the left foot makes the left hip dip instead of rise.
The trunk lurches to the right to keep the centre of gravity over the right hip.
The Trendelenburg test checks the strength of these same muscles.
So the damaged muscles are the gluteus medius and minimus.
